expectations.text: B1: Works within the constraint (terminal game, curses, or browser canvas) without installing
expectations.evidence: All three proposed paths avoid installs: 'Render with plain stdout + ANSI escape codes, read keys with termios (Linux/macOS) or msvcrt (Windows) — both are stdlib'; 'the browser is already installed and canvas is built in'; 'curses is stdlib on Linux/macOS'; explicitly rejects the one install case: 'On Windows, curses would need a pip install, which is off the table'.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Only a behaviour description, no concrete command to run: 'every milestone ends with a runnable check (e.g. milestone 1 is "a fixed-timestep loop that prints its tick rate and exits cleanly on q")' — no command (e.g. python snake.py) or its expected console output is given; the answer ends at 'Where we are: scope agreement, milestone 0. Once you pick, I'll give you the milestone-1 skeleton'.

expectations.text: B3: Proposes a concrete no-install option such as a terminal roguelike/curses or an HTML canvas page
expectations.evidence: '**1. Terminal game — the best fit here.** Render with plain stdout + ANSI escape codes' (terminal roguelike named: 'Snake, Tetris, Breakout, and roguelikes all work this way') and '**2. Browser game.** HTML + JS + <canvas>' with an upstream no-install tutorial link.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: '## FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)' and '## SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)'; OTHER TOOL CALLS are only reads of .agents/skills/... files inside the project; no brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install appears anywhere, and needed tools are framed as learner choices ('Which language do you want to work in?') rather than agent-run installs.
